title: Zero-width code point inserted inside a credential
summary: A single U+200B (ZERO WIDTH SPACE), U+200C, U+200D or U+2060 inserted inside an otherwise intact synthetic key.
rationale: Each inserted code point is outside the documented-grammar alphabet of both families, so no issued key contains it; it is a transformation of the key, recorded as insert-codepoints with a strip-codepoints decode of exactly the inserted code points. Removing every invisible character from a text is not assumed to preserve other values (see unicode-format-characters-in-benign-text), so the decode step names what was inserted.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, decided here as a research position and open to maintainer review: when exactly the inserted zero-width code points, removed, give a documented-grammar key, the key bytes (UTF-8 offsets, including the inserted code points inside the span) are the secret. Question: does an invisible inside a key make it a different value? Options: (a) the inserted code point is not part of the secret and the key is still present; (b) a different, non-credential string. Chosen: (a), because no issued key contains the code point and a copy from a rendered page is the realistic origin. Reverse if a provider states that keys may be rejected or altered by such characters, or a maintainer chooses (b).

sources.supports: Section 3 table: U+0800-U+FFFF encodes as three bytes and U+10000-U+10FFFF as four, so every zero-width, BOM and emoji offset shift in these fixtures is derivable from the code point.
The key is documented as always 69 characters; the alphabet and 22/43 segment split are tool-corroborated, not this citation. Context only: it does not mention Unicode.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Research for #96 (parent #92). Synthetic fixtures only; input facts and expectations live here, while stream APIs, limits, actual output and rejection assertions belong to downstream engine and product regression populations.
